title: Tangier International Zone
capsule: The Tangier International Zone was a demilitarized and internationalized port enclave in northern Morocco, formally established by the Paris Convention of 18 December 1923 and operative from 1 June 1925 under joint administration by France, Spain, Britain, and later other powers. Governed by a Committee of Control (the participating consuls), a Legislative Assembly, Mixed Courts, and a Mendoub (the Sultan's representative), the Zone functioned as a tax haven with no tariffs, no income tax, and no exchange controls, hosting eighty-five banks by 1950 and attracting cosmopolitan expatriate and nationalist circles. Spain occupied and annexed it to the Spanish Protectorate on 14 June 1940, restoring international status only in October 1945. Following Moroccan independence, a protocol of 29 October 1956 ended the special regime and reintegrated Tangier into the Kingdom of Morocco.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Zone's boundaries were precisely defined by international treaty and correspond to a known urban perimeter; territorial extent is well-documented.
